By 1925 Samitier was the highest-paid player in [Spain](/wiki/Football_in_Spain "Football in Spain"). He was a member of the legendary [FC Barcelona](/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") team, coached by [Jack Greenwell](/wiki/Jack_Greenwell "Jack Greenwell"), that, apart from Sagibarba, also included [Paulino Alcántara](/wiki/Paulino_Alc%C3%A1ntara "Paulino Alcántara"), [Ricardo Zamora](/wiki/Ricardo_Zamora "Ricardo Zamora"), [Félix Sesúmaga](/wiki/F%C3%A9lix_Ses%C3%BAmaga "Félix Sesúmaga") and, later, [Franz Platko](/wiki/Franz_Platko "Franz Platko"). Between 1919 and 1933 he won twelve [Campionat de Catalunya](/wiki/Catalan_football_championship "Catalan football championship") titles, five [Copa del Rey](/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey") and the very first [La Liga](/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") title in the [1929 season](/wiki/La_Liga_1929 "La Liga 1929"). Among the goals he scored were four in the [Copa del Rey](/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey") finals of 1922, 1925, 1926 and 1928.

Australia :: Demographics :: Health :: chunk_0031
See also: [Health care in Australia](/wiki/Health_care_in_Australia "Health care in Australia")

Australia's life expectancy of 83 years (81 years for males and 85 years for females)[[325]](#cite_note-336) is the [fifth-highest in the world](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy "List of countries by life expectancy"). It has the highest rate of skin cancer in the world,[[326]](#cite_note-337) while [cigarette smoking](/wiki/Tobacco_smoking "Tobacco smoking") is the largest preventable cause of death and disease, responsible for 7.8% of the total mortality and disease. Ranked second in preventable causes is [hypertension](/wiki/Hypertension "Hypertension") at 7.6%, with obesity third at 7.5%.[[327]](#cite_note-338)[[328]](#cite_note-339) Australia ranked 35th in the world in 2012 for its proportion of obese women[[329]](#cite_note-340) and near the top of [developed nations](/wiki/Developed_country "Developed country") for its proportion of [obese](/wiki/Obesity_in_Australia "Obesity in Australia") adults;[[330]](#cite_note-341) 63% of its adult population is either overweight or obese.[[331]](#cite_note-342)

Australia spent about 9.91% of its total GDP to health care in 2021.[[332]](#cite_note-343) It introduced a [national insurance scheme](/wiki/National_health_insurance "National health insurance") in 1975.[[333]](#cite_note-Biggs-2004-344) Following a period in which access to the scheme was restricted, the scheme became [universal](/wiki/Universal_health_care "Universal health care") once more in 1981 under the name of [Medicare](/wiki/Medicare_(Australia) "Medicare (Australia)").[[334]](#cite_note-345) The program is nominally funded by an income tax surcharge known as the [Medicare levy](/wiki/Medicare_levy "Medicare levy"), currently at 2%.[[335]](#cite_note-346) The states manage hospitals and attached outpatient services, while the Commonwealth funds the [Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme](/wiki/Pharmaceutical_Benefits_Scheme "Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme") (subsidising the costs of medicines) and [general practice](/wiki/General_practice "General practice").[[333]](#cite_note-Biggs-2004-344)

Armstrong was born in rural [Washington Township](/wiki/Washington_Township,_Auglaize_County,_Ohio "Washington Township, Auglaize County, Ohio"), in [Auglaize County, Ohio](/wiki/Auglaize_County,_Ohio "Auglaize County, Ohio"),[[5]](#cite_note-5) on August 5, 1930, the son of Viola Louise (née Engel) and Stephen Koenig Armstrong. He was of German, English, Scots-Irish, Irish, and Scottish descent.[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen200513,_20-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8) He is a descendant of [Clan Armstrong](/wiki/Clan_Armstrong "Clan Armstrong").[[9]](#cite_note-9) He had a younger sister, June, and a younger brother, Dean. His father was an [auditor](/wiki/Auditor "Auditor") for the [Ohio state government](/wiki/Government_of_Ohio "Government of Ohio"),[[10]](#cite_note-10) and the family moved around the state repeatedly, living in 16 towns over the next 14 years.[[11]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen200529-11) Armstrong's love for flying grew during this time, having started at the age of two when his father took him to the [Cleveland Air Races](/wiki/National_Air_Races "National Air Races"). When he was five or six, he experienced his first airplane flight in [Warren, Ohio](/wiki/Warren,_Ohio "Warren, Ohio"), when he and his father took a ride in a [Ford Trimotor](/wiki/Ford_Trimotor "Ford Trimotor") (also known as the "Tin Goose").[[12]](#cite_note-12)[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen200545-13) Armstrong constructed and flew model aircraft, beginning in his youth.[[14]](#cite_note-14)

The family's last move was in 1944 and took them back to Wapakoneta, where Armstrong attended [Blume High School](/wiki/Blume_High_School "Blume High School") and took flying lessons at the Wapakoneta airfield.[[15]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen200549–50-15) He earned a student flight certificate on his 16th birthday, then [soloed](/wiki/First_solo_flight "First solo flight") in August, all before he had a driver's license.[[16]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKoestler-Grack201014-16) He was an active [Boy Scout](/wiki/Boy_Scouts_of_America "Boy Scouts of America") and earned the rank of [Eagle Scout](/wiki/Eagle_Scout_(Boy_Scouts_of
